Warehouse transfer

Move a quantity of one item from one warehouse to another in the same company, and check the stock at both.

Before you start

  • An item with stock in one warehouse, and a second warehouse of the same company to move it to. To find where the item has stock, follow Check an item's inventory.

Procedure

1Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type

Result
The on-hand at both warehouses and the expected order type are written down.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing changes yet. A transfer is checked at both ends, so you need the stock at both warehouses before you start. The order type a transfer gets comes from Default Order Types by Origin, and that type's warehousing procedure decides which later steps LN runs by itself.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Type the item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it
1.2Tick the item's own rowThe header links become available
1.3In the Inventory group, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory (whwmd2515m000) opens with the item already filled inWrite downitemsource warehousesource on-hand before
1.4In the same grid, find the row for the warehouse you're moving the goods toWrite downdestination warehousedestination on-hand before
1.5Open Warehousing➔Master Data➔Order Procedures➔Default Order Types by Origin (whinh0120m000)The table of default order types opens
1.6Use the toolbar's next and previous arrows until Order Origin reads Transfer (Manual). Then find the row with transaction type Transfer, ship-from Warehouse and ship-to WarehouseWrite downexpected warehousing order typeCreate Shipment. Between two different warehouses, Infor's help says Create Shipment is Always

2Create the transfer order

Result
The transfer order is saved with transaction type Transfer and one line for the item.
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders (whinh2100m000)

Why LN works this way. A warehousing order you enter by hand has no sales or purchase order behind it, so its number comes from Warehousing's own number group. LN fills in the origin, the transaction type and the order type, and you check them. For a transfer inside one company, LN puts both halves of the move on this one order: the outbound and shipment steps, then the inbound and inspection steps.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Warehousing➔Orders➔OrdersWarehousing Orders (whinh2100m000) opens
2.2Click NewWarehousing Order (whinh2100m100) opens with the origin, transaction type and order type already filled in
2.3Check that the order's origin reads Transfer (Manual)
2.4Check that Transaction Type reads Transfer
2.5Set Ship-From Code to the source warehouse from step 1.3
2.6Set Ship-To Code to the destination warehouse from step 1.4Both types read Warehouse, which a Transfer needs
2.7Compare the Warehousing Order Type LN filled in with the one from step 1.6ExampleWarehousing Order Type 45= — Transfer (Internal), which LN fills in
2.8Write down the order type the order actually hasWrite downactual warehousing order type
2.9Save the headerWrite downtransfer order number
2.10Add an order line with the item from step 1.3
2.11Enter the quantity to move as Ordered QuantityExampleOrdered Quantity 10Write downtransferred quantity
2.12Save the line
Create the transfer order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No order number appearsThe header isn't saved, or a required field is still empty. Check steps 2.3 to 8 again
What you type in the ship-to warehouse box is lostWith LN's menu panel open, that box can sit past the window's edge. Hide the panel with the menu button at the top left, then type it again

3Confirm the processing path and create advice

Result
The outbound line reads Released or later, and the activities that are yours are written down.
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Outbound Line Status Overview (whinh2129m000)

Why LN works this way. The order type brought a default procedure, and the order or its line may have changed it. The activity table on the line is the only place that says which steps LN runs by itself and which are yours. Read it before you generate advice: guessing from the item is how a step gets done twice or missed.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open Outbound Line Status Overview (whinh2129m000)The overview of outbound lines opens
3.2Filter Order on the order from Create the transfer order, tick its line and click Drill InThe line's detail opens. The item and order line match, and Order Type matches the one from step 2.8
3.3Read every row in the Activities table, above all Finished and AutomaticAutomatic Yes means LN runs it; No means you do
3.4Write down the activities whose Automatic is NoWrite downmanual outbound activities. These are the later steps you'll carry out
3.5If the next activity is automatic, choose Process on the warehousing orderLN runs the automatic activities in a row and stops at the next one that's yours
3.6If Generate Outbound Advice is yours, open Outbound Lines and select the line
3.7Choose Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceAdvised fills in. Automatic steps after it may finish too
3.8If Release Outbound Advice is yours and Released is still empty, choose Actions➔Advice➔Release AdviceReleased fills in
Confirm the processing path and create advice: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Advice is greyed outYou may be on the screen's own toolbar, not the Outbound Lines toolbar. See step 3.6

4Pick the goods

Result
The outbound line reads Picked or later.
Screen
Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List (whinh4525m100)

Why LN works this way. Picking is an activity only in a location-controlled warehouse, and a step of yours only where the procedure says so. Otherwise Picked fills in without you. It works the same way as picking for a sale, on the transfer's own outbound line.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Find the Picking List row you read at step 3.3If it isn't there, or LN already finished it, write down Automatic / not applicable and skip steps 4.2 to 5. If its Automatic is No, carry on
4.2Find the run for this orderThe line for your item and source warehouse
4.3Tick the line
4.4Choose Actions➔Pick RunThe stock moves from its location to staging, and Picked fills in on Outbound Lines
4.5Write down the run number from the headerWrite downpicking list run number
Pick the goods: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No run appears on the Picking ListIf the order has already moved on, write down Automatic / not observed. Otherwise picking may not apply, or advice wasn't generated. Go back to Confirm the processing path and create advice

5Ship

Result
The outbound line reads Shipped.
Screen
Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments (whinh4130m000)

Why LN works this way. A transfer between two different warehouses always creates a shipment; only a transfer within one warehouse doesn't. Whether you freeze and confirm the shipment, or the procedure does, is in the activity table you read in Confirm the processing path and create advice.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Find the Freeze/Confirm Shipments/Loads row you read at step 3.3If LN already finished it, write down Automatic / not observed and skip steps 5.2 to 4. If its Automatic is No, carry on
5.2Find the shipment for this order and click Drill InWrite downshipment number
5.3If Freeze Mandatory is ticked, choose Actions➔FreezeStatus = Frozen
5.4Choose Actions➔ConfirmStatus = Confirmed, and the goods leave the source warehouse
Ship: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No shipment shows for a transfer between two warehousesInfor's help says Create Shipment is Always. Check Shipment Lines and the activity table from Confirm the processing path and create advice before going on
Confirm is greyed outThe shipment may not be frozen yet. Run step 5.3 first

6Receive at the destination

Result
The receipt reads Confirmed.

Why LN works this way. The same order now runs its inbound half. Every inbound line needs a receipt and inbound advice, and a transfer's inbound lines are received and confirmed on the same receipt screen a purchase uses. Confirming the receipt is what puts the goods into the destination warehouse.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Open the Inbound Lines tab on the transfer orderThe inbound side of the same order, with the destination warehouse as ship-to
6.2Tick the inbound line and choose Actions➔Receive…Warehouse Receipt (whinh3512m000) opens with a receipt for the destination warehouse, and the line's full quantity already received
6.3Tick the receipt line and choose Actions➔ConfirmThe receipt reads Confirmed, and the destination's stock goes up

7Verify it worked

Result
The source fell and the destination rose by the transferred quantity, once anything else that moved the item is allowed for.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing new. A transfer is checked twice: the source down and the destination up by the same quantity. One half can hold while the other doesn't, so this task reads both.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Read the item's on-hand at both warehouses, in the same view as step 1.3Write downsource on-hand afterdestination on-hand after

The source should be down by the transferred quantity, and the destination up by the same quantity, as long as nothing else moved the item in either warehouse. The transfer is done only when both hold.

Verify it worked: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The destination's on-hand didn't go upThe receipt in Receive at the destination may not be confirmed. Go back to the inbound line and Warehouse Receipt
The two changes don't both equal the transferred quantitySomething else may have moved the item. Check the figures from Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type and look for other movements of the item before trusting the result

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Multicompany warehouse transfer — source and destination warehouses in different logistic companiesLN generates two warehousing orders instead of one: the ship-from company's order carries the outbound and shipment activities, the ship-to company's carries inbound and inspection. Ship-to Code becomes meaningful. This changes the tasks (an order handoff is needed) and earns its own process rather than a row here
Planned/automated transfer, driven by Order PlanningTransfer Order Planning (cppat1210m000), reached via Planning➔Plan Transfer➔Transfer Order Planning, generates transfer orders from planned inventory transactions rather than a person entering one by hand. Out of scope for this process.
Serialized or lot-controlled itemThe order header's Reclassification tab applies to rental and serialized transfers specifically. This variant is outside the scope of this process
